title: Turn scores into a loss with a readable gradient
brief: Write a stable softmax, a stable log-softmax, and the cross-entropy loss whose slope on the scores is predicted probabilities minus the truth.
hints: softmax: subtract each row's maximum with keepdims=True, exponentiate, then divide by the row sum. The shift changes no probability and keeps exp from overflowing.
log_softmax: (z - m) - log(sum(exp(z - m))) for the same shift m. Do not take log of softmax(z), because small probabilities underflow to 0.
In softmax_cross_entropy, pick each row's correct entry with log_probs[np.arange(n), labels]. Indexing with [:, labels] gives an (n, n) block.
The slope on the logits is (softmax(z) - one_hot(labels)) / n. Subtract 1 at the correct entry of each row, then divide by n because the loss is a mean.
